Subject: Data retention exception - follow-up from call

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard:
- FinTechCo needs a data retention exception for certain request logs that may contain PII (payment tokens, partial SSNs)
- Primary ask: 0-retention (no request/response persistence) for PII-containing requests, or alternatively a shortened retention window and redaction
- Compliance wants to understand what minimal telemetry Redwood needs for fraud detection / abuse prevention and billing reconciliation

Proposed options (high-level):
1) Hosted API + DPA with redaction pipeline: we can configure request redaction and shortened request/response retention (e.g., 7 days) for PII, but Hosted retains minimal telemetry for monitoring (see notes)
2) Dedicated/Private deployment: we can provide 0-retention for request/response logs (no persistent storage) when deployed in customer-managed VPC or Dedicated cluster with agreed config
3) Hybrid: short retention (7 days) for request metadata + 0-retention for full request/response payloads; audit logs retained separately (default 90 days) with access controls

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm FinTechCo legal's preferred outcome (0-retention vs shortened retention)?
- If they want 0-retention, can they share a redline or SA with specific clauses we should review?
- I attached a draft DPA we typically start with; Rafael will coordinate scoping and pricing if Dedicated/private is required.

Attachment: redwood_dpa_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48KB)

If it helps, we can set up a legal-to-legal call next week to walk through the redlines. Happy to coordinate times.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. FinTechCo's security and compliance bar is strict: our legal team is asking for 0-retention of request/response payloads that include PII. We understand telemetry for fraud detection is important, but we need to limit any stored payloads that could contain customer data.

I've asked our security lead to attach the SA with the redlines we typically push for — see attached. Our preference:
- No persistent storage of full request/response payloads containing PII
- If logs are needed for operational reasons, they must be redacted on ingest and retained no longer than 7 days
- Audit logs (access records) can be retained for 90 days under strict access controls

Attachment: FinTechCo_SA-DataRetention_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

Can Redwood confirm whether 0-retention is possible on the Hosted API, and if not, what the pathway and costs are for Dedicated/Private to meet our needs? Also please indicate any minimal telemetry you require and whether it can be limited to hashed identifiers only.

Thanks —
Alex

Hi Alex / FinTechCo legal —

Thanks for the SA redlines. Quick answers and where we suggest taking this next: 

Hosted API:
- Our Hosted product retains request/response logs for a short period to support streaming, debugging, and abuse detection. We can enable aggressive redaction and a shortened retention window (e.g., 7 days) for PII-containing fields, and we support hashing/pseudonymization of identifiers. However, we cannot currently provide a true 0-retention guarantee on the Hosted environment because of shared infrastructure and monitoring requirements.

Dedicated / Private Deployment:
- With a Dedicated pool or Private deployment, we can configure the runtime and storage policies to avoid persistent request/response storage entirely (0-retention) for specified routes. This configuration is supported, subject to an architecture review and a deployment-scoped DPA amendment. There is typically an increase in cost (reserved capacity + configuration/ops) to support this mode.

Minimal telemetry:
- For fraud/abuse detection we require minimal metadata: request timestamp, route id, success/failure code, tokenized/hashed identifier. We can avoid storing raw payloads or any PII values if you prefer. Billing reconciliation uses aggregated token counts only — no payloads.

Suggested next steps:
1) Legal-to-legal call to walk through the SA redlines and the DPA draft I attached earlier. I can have our legal and security leads join.
2) If FinTechCo wants 0-retention, Rafael will scope Dedicated/Private options and provide a pricing estimate and timeline.
3) If you prefer Hosted with hardened redaction, we can provide a technical design doc that shows how we'd redact and enforce retention windows.

I've attached the DPA draft for your review again and linked our retention options in the doc.

Attachment: redwood_dpa_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48KB)
Related link: https://docs.redwood.com/data-retention#options

Let me know available times for a call next week; Rafael will follow up on pricing if Dedicated is required.

Best,

Marissa
